title: Tech Note: Returning Pictures Through SOAP

historical_commentary.text: This note solves a specific early SOAP limitation: 4D's Web Services responses supported nearly every native data type except pictures directly, requiring a picture-to-BLOB conversion workaround to transmit images over SOAP/XML. That workaround is entirely tied to 4D's now largely legacy SOAP Web Services stack; modern 4D applications needing to serve images over an API overwhelmingly use REST/JSON endpoints (returning binary data, base64, or URLs) rather than SOAP-encoded BLOBs, making this note's specific technique of historical interest only, even though the general challenge of transmitting binary image data over structured web protocols remains a recognizable problem class.
related_updates: 4D's web services capabilities have expanded to REST/JSON, which is now the dominant approach for serving images/binary data over HTTP APIs rather than SOAP+BLOB encoding
SOAP-based Web Services are largely legacy technology in current 4D development
